Metadata.Title: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
Metadata.Name: Post shading at render size
Metadata.Note: For the Bachata 'N render, 1080p output' resolution patches: UpdatePostProcessingCsConst (post-shading-win.cpp) takes the display size (display configuration +0x24/+0x28) for the post-processing compute constants: the 8x8 light tile grid (U1's tiled lighting, cs 43b8ee5e), 128x64 blocks and 1/size. With a smaller scene the lights land in the wrong tiles (blocky projected light of the temple lanterns). These reads take the scene size (+0x18/+0x1c) instead.
Metadata.Author: uncharted-g2

Metadata.Title: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
Metadata.Name: Movie chroma plane at 1920x1088
Metadata.Note: For the full resolution patches (output below 1080p) with the S4+ movie texture lines (@0x9de4fe/53d/597/5db) instead of their @0x8fb7b1 line: the movie renderer (movie-rendering.cpp) finds the decoded frame's chroma plane at displaySize.w * AlignUp(displaySize.h, 64); movies are 1920x1080, so it is pinned to 1920 * 1088. Unlike @0x8fb7b1 the YUV-to-RGB dispatch keeps the display size (no writes past the display buffer). With the port's BB_VDEC_CONTENT set to the output size the whole movie shows.
Metadata.Author: uncharted-g2

Metadata.Title: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
Metadata.Name: Job workers sleep when idle
Metadata.Note: The job system's six NdJobWorkerThreads wait for work by spinning (pause) at the lowest priority, 767, during gameplay: on PS4 any other thread takes the core first, on Android they took cores from the port's GPU threads. The game has a sleep mode of its own (flag [ctx+0x59], set only while loading: after 1000 spins Lock / Wait(10 ms) / Unlock, and adding a job Broadcasts). These lines make it unconditional and cut the spins before sleeping to 64. Resumed fibers do not Broadcast: the worker that resumed one usually runs it, otherwise the 10 ms wait bounds the delay. Same code in U2 and U3.
Metadata.Author: uncharted-android

Metadata.Title: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
Metadata.Name: Job workers wait 1 ms when idle
Metadata.Note: Goes with "Job workers sleep when idle": the idle wait (scePthreadCondTimedwait on ctx+0x80) times out after 1 ms instead of 10 ms, so work nobody signals (a resumed fiber) waits at most 1 ms. Same code in U2 and U3.
Metadata.Author: uncharted-android

Metadata.Title: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
Metadata.Name: Idle job workers sleep 50 us between checks
Metadata.Note: Instead of the sleep mode. An idle worker checks its queues, then spins with a pause (@0x85d26f, @0x85d276); in our FEX a pause is a wfe that waits up to ~100 us for the event stream but keeps the core, so six idle workers hold six cores the render threads need. Here the pause is sceKernelUsleep(50) (PLT @0xb68f00; a nanosleep, ~100 us with the timer slack): the same check interval, the core free meanwhile, no condition variable to miss. The call is in the block @0x85d281 that reported a failed lock of the sleepers' mutex (r11 kept in its slot at rbp-0x60). Same code in U2 and U3.
Metadata.Author: uncharted-android

Metadata.Title: Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection
Metadata.Name: Uncharted 1: Job counter waits also end below their target
Metadata.Note: A wait of the job manager for a counter to equal its target (mode 0: WaitForCounter, the waiting job entries, the job lists whose start waits, the worker's checks, the fiber wait) also ends when the counter is below the target, as mode 1 (value <= target) does: one opcode byte at each of the 12 places (sete -> setle, jne -> jl or jg). Counters only count down to their targets, so the two tests differ only for a counter decremented once too often - a job of an earlier use of the counter object finishing late: the waiter that checks after the extra decrement then waits for ever (notes/findings.md 2026-10-28, 2026-10-29). The same job manager code as U2's (its places found by the bytes around each).
Metadata.Author: uncharted-android
